headline: Approved changes to the pension plan's assumptions, a new parking fund, and a parking ban on East Terrace.
summary: The Council heard a five-year strategic plan from the Library Board and discussed its legislative priorities for 2027-2028. It also met in executive session on labor agreements with the firefighters' association and possible regional service contracts.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda without item c, unanimously.
Approved Resolution 2026-17 creating a parking fund, 4-1.
Approved a ban on parking on the East side of East Terrace from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., Monday through Friday, and moved Central Avenue parking to the East side, unanimously.
Approved changes to the South Burlington Pension Plan's assumptions and valuation methods, unanimously.

PAGE 1 
DRAFT MINUTES 
 CITY COUNCIL 
     16 NOVEMBER 2026 
 
The South Burlington City Council held a regular meeting on Monday, 16 
November 2026, at 6:30 p.m., in the Auditorium, 180 Market Street, and by Zoom. 
 
MEMBERS PRESENT: T. Barritt, Chair; E. Fitzgerald, L. Smith, A. Chalnick, Dr. B. 
Zigmund 
 
ALSO PRESENT: J. Baker, City Manager; N. Storellicastro, Deputy City Manager; E. 
Towle, Director of Public Works; T. Lenski, W. Kirzinger, A. Lalonde, Library Board 
of Trustees; M. Machar, Finance Director; C. Atherton, N. Atherton, R. Pyle, A, E, & 
T. Treston, J. Materna, S. Julius, P. Vashishta, J. Crome, R. Curtis, K. Ward, J. 
Sterbank, L. Scherer, R. Doyle, D. Swartwout   
 
1. Pledge of Allegiance: 
 
The Pledge of Allegiance was recited. 
 
2. Instructions on exiting building in case of emergency and review of 
technology options: 
 
Ms. Baker provided instructions on emergency exit from the building and 
reviewed technology options. 
  
3. Additions, deletions or changes in the order of Agenda items: 
 
No changes were made to the Agenda. 
 
4. Comments and questions from the public not related to the agenda: 
 
No issues were raised.
CITY COUNCIL 16 November 2026 PAGE 2 
5. Councilors Announcements and Reports on Committee Assignments                                                        
and City Manager’s Report: 
 
Council members reported on recent meetings and events they had attended. 
 
Members noted the passing of John Kilacky, former State Legislator and 
champion of the arts. 
 
Ms. Baker: Noted the success of the Hearth Market. 
 
                 Noted the passing of Thom Lauzon, Mayor of Barre, and long-time 
champion of his community. 
 
      Spotlight 802 this week will highlight the Beta story. 
 
Ms. Fitzgerald asked if there have been any ramifications regarding the Microsoft 
outage. Ms. Baker said emails backed up, but there were no other impacts to the 
system. 
 
6. Consent Agenda: 
a. Consider and Sign Disbursements 
b. Accept infrastructure: Garden Street, Stormwater Maintenance 
Agreement for Garden Street, Foulsham Hollow Road, and Tilley 
Drive Right-of-Way 
c. Approve Resolution 2026-17 creating a parking fund 
d. Approve Resolution 2026-18 to adjust parking ticket fees 
e. Approve the Code of Conduct for 180 Market Street 
f. Reappoint Tim Barritt and Laurie Smith to serve as the City’s 
representative and alternate (respectively) to the Chittenden 
County Communications Union District for a period of two years 
g. Receive August financials 
h. Approve minutes from 22 September 2026 and 5 October 2026 
City Council meetings 
 
Mr. Chalnick asked to pull item “c” from the Consent Agenda. 
 
Mr. Smith moved to approve the Consent Agenda minus item “c” as presented.  
Dr. Zigmund seconded.  Motion passed unanimously.
CITY COUNCIL 16 November 2026 PAGE 3 
Mr. Chalnick said he felt that merging the parking fund with parking tickets felt 
awkward to him.  He said that what is garnered from tickets should go into the 
General Fund.   
 
Ms. Baker said the parking fund would function as a utility.  She also noted that 
later in the agenda, the Council will be presented with an item to change parking 
fees.  She added that in other cities, the parking fund has been self-sustaining 
though she felt the City was a few years away from that. 
 
Dr. Zigmund asked if there is a “best practices.”  She said it seems to be clear to 
see what is coming in and what is going out.   
 
Mr. Smith then moved to approve item “c” of the Consent Agenda.  Dr. Zigmund 
seconded.  The motion passed 4-1 with Ms. Fitzgerald voting against. 
 
7. Consider approving Resolution #2026-19 updating on street parking: 
 
Ms. Towle said this is a follow-up to residents coming to the City Council.  The 
Resolution clarifies parking only on the West side of East Terrace and includes 
some technical updates. 
 
Mr. Barritt asked where the flashing “no parking” lights are located.  Ms. Towle 
said they are tucked into the jug handle.  She wasn’t sure when they flashed. 
 
Mr. Smith said parking should be on the East side of Queen City Park Road as Red 
Rocks Park is on the West side.  Ms. Towle said that is correct and it is an 
amendment. 
 
Ms. Treston said the amendment regarding East Terrace does not remove the 
time restrictions.  She added it is very difficult for children to use the cross-walk 
and for drivers to leave their driveways.   
 
Ms. Pyle said there is a very old “No Parking 6 a.m. to 6 p.m.” sign in front of her 
house, and the City would make a lot of money if it enforced that. 
 
Ms. Atherton suggested having the “No Parking” signs on the side of the street 
where there are sidewalks. Ms. Towle said they went back and forth on this, 
looked at aerial imagery, etc., and there are good reasons for both sides.  Ms. 
Atherton said with the Tarrant Center now going to be built, there should be
CITY COUNCIL 16 November 2026 PAGE 4 
something in place now.  She suggested having the east side of the street for 
“resident parking only.”   
 
Mr. Crome suggested just enforcing what is already there. 
 
Mr. Smith then moved to ban parking on the East side of East Terrace from 6 a.m. 
to 6 p.m. Monday through Friday and to correct parking on Central Avenue to the 
East side of the street.  Dr. Zigmund seconded.  The motion passed unanimously. 
 
8. Receive a presentation from the Library Board of Trustees on their 5-
year Strategic Plan: 
 
Mr. Lenski thanked the Council for appointing amazing people to the Library 
Board.  He said their 5-year Strategic Plan was internally developed and approved 
by the Board.  The process included brainstorming sessions and then reducing the 
200 ideas generated into 25 high areas and then 6 priorities.  The key focus was to 
align with the City Plan, and the proposed Strategic Plan does align with 6 goals 
and 6 actions in the City Plan. 
 
Ms. Lalonde then outlined the 4 main pillars of the plan as follows: 
 
 #1. Library Spaces: ensure the Library provides the spaces the community 
needs 
 
 #2. Welcoming: The Library should be welcoming for all and should meet 
community needs 20 years into the future 
 
 #3. Community Engagement: The Library should inspire community 
members to keep learning and should encourage a diversity of patronage 
 
 #4. The Library should support community well-being. 
 
Ms. Kirzinger said there are 2 to 4 objective for each goal including staff training, a 
positive workplace culture, variety of programs, positioning the Library as a hub 
and broadening its reach, improving access to resources, etc. 
 
Mr. Lenski cited the excellent Library staff and stressed that the Board does not 
tell them what to do.
CITY COUNCIL 16 November 2026 PAGE 5 
Mr. Barritt noted that when the Council voted in 2018, Ms. Riehle and Ms. Emery 
were adamant that the Library would be the cultural center of City Center.   
 
Ms. Fitzgerald asked the difference between the goals of the Library Foundation 
and the Friends of the Library.  Ms. Lalonde said the Friends are more geared to 
providing funds for specific things.   She noted the book sale raised almost $5,000.  
The Foundation raises money through an appeal twice a year and casts a broader 
net.  Mr. Lenski noted that the New York Times was a donation from the 
Foundation, and everyone in the City has access to it.  Ms. Baker added that the 
Foundation also updates the Memorandum of Understanding with the City. 
 
Mr. Barritt asked about the Blanchett Fund.  Mr. Lenski said that has been fully 
used. 
 
Council members praised the work of the Board in creating their plan. 
9. Receive an actuarial update on the South Burlington Pension Plan 
and approve changes to the assumptions and methodology used for 
the valuation of the plan as recommended by the Actuarial 
Consultant: 
 
Ms. Machar introduced Mr. Scherer and Ms. Sterbank, the plans actuaries. 
 
Ms. Sterbank said the plan did well in the prior year.  $950,000 was contributed by 
the City.  Those receiving payments increased, and there were fewer early 
retirements and fewer deaths than anticipated.   
 
This year, the funded percentage decreased to 90%.  Ms. Sterbank showed a 
graph of participant statistics (197 participants with 105 in payment status).  She 
also showed a graph of Funding Results.  There is a $5,100,000 unfunded liability; 
however, a market value of $56,900,000 puts the plan in a fully funded position at 
101%. 
 
Mr. Scherer then outlined their recommendations as follows: 
 
a. Mortality Assumption: They used the most up-to-date Mortality 
Table.  People are tending to live longer, and the longer they live, 
the more costs increase; however, it may also lessen future 
mortality related demographic losses.  It is assumed that Public 
Safety employees will not live as long as others)
CITY COUNCIL 16 November 2026 PAGE 6 
b. Discount Rate: They are currently using a rate of 7.25%.  The 
3year, 5 year and 10 year experience has been higher than that.  
For this reason, they are suggesting lowering the rate to 7%.  This 
is the median of State employees and VMERS. 
 
c. Asset Smoothing Methodology: The recommendation is to reset 
the method with updated mortality and discount rate assumptions 
to help offset significant increases. 
 
Mr. Scherer showed a chart of Assumptions/Methodology Impact on Preliminary 
Results which would reduce the unfunded amount to $3,000,000. 
 
Dr. Zigmund asked what this means for the city’s budget.  Ms. Machar said she 
supports the proposal to contribute $889,000 in the upcoming budget. 
 
Ms. Fitzgerald asked the benchmark that is used to determine the health of the 
plan.  Mr. Scherer said anything about 80% is OK.  Something in the 90’s is very 
strong.  He added that the South Burlington Plan is at a very strong funded level.   
 
Mr. Barritt reminded members that this is a closed plan. 
 
Mr. Chalnick moved to approve the changes to the Pension Plan as presented.  Dr. 
Zigmund seconded.  Motion passed unanimously. 
 
10. Legislative Advocacy Agenda: Discuss Council priorities for 2027-
2028 Biennium and possibly approve: 
 
Ms. Baker reviewed previous discussions.  She stressed that the professionals will 
still provide testimony relative to their expertise.  
 
Regarding possible local option tax expansion, Mr. Barritt said it would be great if 
they could get more information on where the money is coming from.  Mr. 
Chalnick asked if there is any chance of that.  Ms. Baker said that is what VLCT will 
be pushing for.  She stressed there will be lots of threads to that discussion.   Ms. 
Fitzgerald said it sounds more feasible to her to go with something on the State 
level which might result in the City getting more of what is collected.   
 
Mr. Chalnick said he would support that.  He did not want to go from 1% to 2%.  
Mr. Barritt asked if he would support an increase in the rooms/meals tax.  Mr.
CITY COUNCIL 16 November 2026 PAGE 7 
Chalnick said that is more targeting to tourists/visitors.  Ms. Baker reminded 
members that this would require a Charter change. 
 
Mr. Smith said he would look to make a tax more progressive so that people 
struggling to meet necessities are helped.  He felt this is critical for a big segment 
of the community.   
 
Mr. Barritt spoke to the need to know the categories of where local option tax 
money is coming from (e.g. bricks and mortar). 
 
Regarding condos, Mr. Chalnick said there is a lot of confusion as to why there 
can’t be condos.  He cited the need to understand the obstacles, then decide how 
to deal with them.   
 
Regarding plastics, Dr. Zigmund said 400,000 tons of plastics are produced each 
year, and this number is expected to double by 2050.  She cited the threat to 
children and to climate change.  She would like to see an ordinance similar to the 
one enacted in New Jersey.  It resulted in less trash to haul, businesses saving 
money and keeping plastics out of the environment.  Mr. Barritt asked if they can 
do this without the State.  Dr. Zigmund said it is the same issue as with pesticides.  
Ms. Baker reviewed the Charter change process and said this could be hard to do 
with a Charter change because it affects many communities.  It may be easier to 
advocate a State-wide ban. 
 
Mr. Smith said they should keep in mind which Legislative committee things go to 
so they don’t overburden any one committee. 
 
Regarding transportation, Ms. Fitzgerald said this is her #2 priority because it is so 
underfunded and affects businesses and lives.   
 
Mr. Smith said he hoped the Legislature would allow municipalities to have speed 
limits below 25 mph as that is too fast for places where people walk.  He noted 
that Burlington is already doing that. 
 
Members supported this. 
 
Regarding studded tires on roads, Mr. Chalnick said a number of state have 
banned them because of road damage.  Mr. Smith said he would like to see data 
on that.  Dr. Zigmund was willing to let it ride.
CITY COUNCIL 16 November 2026 PAGE 8 
Mr. Chalnick asked if the City can enforce energy codes today.  Mr. McNeil said he 
hasn’t dug into this in its entirety.  He would be happy to talk about it off-line. 
 
Regarding conflicts of interest, Mr. Chalnick felt “reasonable conflicts” were OK.  
Mr. Smith said the rules talk away the ability for someone to exercise judgment.  
Mr. Chalnick stressed that Legislators don’t apply this to themselves.  Mr. Barritt 
said there are towns where there are severe conflicts and horrible stories arising 
from them.   
 
Regarding new buildings statewide to be solar ready, Mr. Chalnick said the State 
code does not require roofs to be strong enough to hold solar.  This legislation 
would not do anything for South Burlington as the City already has a code, but it 
would make a difference in the rest of the State.  Dr. Zigmund said if they can’t do 
it with new construction, we are “behind the 8 ball.”   
 
Members agreed to leave it in. 
 
Regarding regulation of e-vehicle sales, 3 members favored leaving it in. 
 
Ms. Fitzgerald cited the need to keep on top of the issue of neighbors appealing 
permits. 
 
11. Discuss the Council’s goals for a vacant building and graffiti 
ordinance: 
 
Mr. Barritt felt that any graffiti on a commercial building that is not removed 
within 30 days should incur a fine.  Ms. Baker requested that the Council focus on 
defining the policy goal they are trying to solve.  Mr. Smith said it would ensure 
that the City doesn’t look “ratty.”  Dr. Zigmund said her goal would be to establish 
an ordinance that relates to property maintenance so there isn’t another Pizza Hut 
building there for 10 years.  Ms. Fitzgerald said if they go this path, it should be to 
protect public health and property values. 
 
Members agreed to put it on the bike rack. 
 
Mr. Doyle noted that the building next to the Middle School has been vacant for 
several years and is a real hazard.  He felt it should be dealt with before 
something bad happens.   
 
It was noted that the building has an association with a Burlington gas station.
CITY COUNCIL 16 November 2026 PAGE 9 
 
12. Discuss standardized communication to residents who contact the 
City Council and staff: 
 
Ms. Fitzgerald said she has heard concerns from residents regarding timeliness of 
responses, forwarding of requests to appropriate departments, awareness of 
operational issues, and residents expectations when brought forward to the 
Council. She felt that there should be some acknowledgment that a concern was 
received and where it was directed. 
 
Mr. Chalnick said he would like to be more aware when there is a neighborhood 
issue. 
 
Ms. Baker stated that she is responsible for City operations and any issues be 
brought to her.  She also stressed that sometimes the Council needs to champion 
an unpopular response from staff.   
 
Mr. Storellicastro said if they receive a request and ask a staff to respond, it is 
taking them away from another priority.  Priority decisions need to be made 
whenever anything comes in. 
 
Mr. Smith said he fully understands that.  He suggested just getting back to the 
person and saying “we will get back to you as soon as possible.” 
 
13. Discuss placing wildlife-friendly (amber) bulbs in the lights at 
Hubbard Park and directing the hours of operation of the lights: 
 
Dr. Zigmund noted that CCRPC’s consultant did a 50-page manual on this.   
 
Mr. Barritt suggested leaving the lights off in the winter and talking about this in 
the spring. 
 
Mr. Smith asked whether they can just questions whether this is possible.  Mr. 
Barritt noted this involves a DRB approval with lighting cut sheets, etc.   
 
Mr. Storellicastro said Public Works has not been able to find timers. 
 
14. Discuss process and reporting improvements for high-value projects:
CITY COUNCIL 16 November 2026 PAGE 10 
Ms. Fitzgerald said her concern began with the Bartlett Bay project but also 
concerns the bike/ped bridge and the TIF.  She outlined three steps she would like 
to see taken: 
 
  #1. At the earliest opportunity, inform the Council regard bids vs. 
estimates 
  #2. Improve estimates 
  #3. Provide an opportunity to discuss alternatives 
  #4. Limit bond votes to the local election 
 
Mr. Barritt stressed that they could not know what the Bartlett Bay situation would 
be until they opened the bids.  Ms. Fitzgerald said no one anticipated that, and 
when it got to the Council, there were no alternatives.  Mr. Smith said the hope is 
that there won’t be surprises in the future. 
 
Mr. Storellicastro said there is a dedicated site for the bridge project.  In terms of 
reporting, it can be followed on the web site.  There is not much to report on 
Bartlett Bay as the project hasn’t yet started.   
 
Dr. Zigmund felt that monthly reporting is too frequent.  Mr. Barritt said they want 
to hear about significant progress. Dr. Zigmund added that they also want to hear 
when the scope of a project changes or when there are issues. 
 
15. Review the significant agenda topics for the Council’s 7 December 
2026 Council meeting: 
 
a. FY28 budget: The City Manager will present the FY28 Budget 
b. Land Development Regulations: Tier 1A process updates 
(including Rare, Threatened, and Endangered Species standards) 
and technical corrections.  Additionally, updates to the bedrock 
standards.  Warn a Public Hearing for 4 January 2027. 
c. Receive the Parks and Open Space Master Plan 
 
16. Other Business: 
 
No other business was brought forth. 
 
17. Consider entering into executive session pursuant to 1 V.S.A. 
Section 313(a)(1)(B) for the purpose of discussing labor relations
CITY COUNCIL 16 November 2026 PAGE 11 
agreements with employees and specifically the South Burlington 
Firefighters Association: and 
 
18. Consider entering into executive session pursuant to 1 V.S.A. 
Section 313(a)(1)(A) for the purpose of discussing contracts and 
specifically contracts related to possible regional service provision: 
 
Dr. Zigmund moved that the Council make a specific finding that premature 
general public knowledge of the Council’s discussion on Labor Agreements with 
Employees and Contracts regarding: 1) South Burlington Career Firefighters’ 
Association; and 2) possible regional service provision clearly place this public 
body at a substantial disadvantage.  Mr. Smith seconded the motion which then 
passed unanimously. 
 
Dr. Zigmund moved that the City Council enter executive session under 1 V.S.A. 
Section 313(a)(1)(B) and (a)(1)(A) for the purpose of discussing Labor Agreements 
with Employees and Contracts regarding: 1) South Burlington Career Firefighters’ 
Association; and 2) possible regional service provision, inviting into the sessions 
Ms. Baker, Mr. Storellicastro, Mr. McNeil, Chief Corbin and Chief Breault.  Mr. 
Smith seconded.  The motion passed unanimously. 
 
The Council entered Executive Session at 9:45 p.m. 
 
Ms. Fitzgerald moved to exit executive session.  Mr. Smith seconded.  The motion 
passed unanimously.   
 
As there was no further business to come before the Council Mr. Chalnick moved 
to adjourn.  Dr. Zigmund seconded.  Motion passed unanimously.  The meeting 
was adjourned at 11:03 p.m. 
 
                                                ________________________, Clerk
